# Spec — #490: Remove deprecated `channel_lan` network + `CHANNEL_NAME` marker (portals rename cleanup)

> NOTE (2026-07-29): written before the `portals/{discord,slack}` → `packages/portal-{discord,slack}` + `packages/portal-sdk` rename; `portals/…` paths below map to those packages.

_Milestone 0.13.0, Phase 1, task 1. Written 2026-07-12 against the current branch
(0.13.0-beta.3 baseline). Source assessment:
[`../assessments/490.md`](../assessments/490.md) — all line references below were
re-verified against the working tree._

## 1. Scope

This task closes ALL remaining-work items from the assessment:

1. **Delete the `channel_lan` network** from
   `packages/skeleton/system/stack/core.compose.yml` (lines 188–192: the 4-line
   deprecation comment + the `channel_lan:` key) and remove the `channel_lan`
   row from the network table in `packages/skeleton/system/stack/README.md`
   (line 67).
2. **Drop `CHANNEL_NAME`** from the portal marker keys in
   `packages/lib/src/control-plane/portals.ts` (line 16), simplify to a single
   `PORTAL_NAME` constant, and update the stale doc comments (lines 64, 99).
3. **Negative test pinning the marker removal** — decided location: a new bun
   test `packages/lib/src/control-plane/portals.test.ts`, NOT the ui vitest
   suite. Rationale: `core-principles.md` § Shared control-plane library —
   "Test coverage for control-plane logic belongs in lib's test suite, not
   duplicated across consumer test suites" — and the milestone gate for this
   task runs `bun run lib:test`, not `ui:test:unit`. The existing
   `packages/ui/src/lib/server/portals.vitest.ts` is left untouched (it only
   uses `PORTAL_NAME` and stays green).
4. **Overlay safety story (decision recorded)** — the issue's "optional" scan,
   made near-mandatory by review finding M7
   (`docs/reviews/upgrade-migration-review-2026-07-06.md:65`: the migration
   framework, including the CHANGELOG-promised `channel_lan`→`portal_net`
   rewrite, was deleted). **DECISION: option (a), a read-only scan — refined
   into a fail-fast preflight guard. Option (b) (auto-rewrite of
   `custom.compose.yml`) is REJECTED.**
   - Why not (b): `custom.compose.yml` lives in the user-owned `config/` tree.
     `core-principles.md` golden rule: "Never overwrite existing user-modified
     files in `~/.openpalm/config/` during automatic lifecycle operations."
     The 0.12.0 rewrite promise was executed by a migration framework that no
     longer exists; re-implementing a one-shot user-file rewriter for a
     removal cleanup is unjustified complexity and contradicts the current
     filesystem contract.
   - Why fail-fast rather than warn-and-proceed: if `custom.compose.yml`
     attaches a service to `channel_lan` and does not define that network
     itself, the merged compose config is invalid the moment the skeleton
     refresh lands — `reconcileCore`'s compose preflight then hard-fails
     mid-operation with a cryptic Docker error, AFTER `applyHome` has already
     overwritten `core.compose.yml` (which is NOT in the crash-restore set of
     `withStackEnvRollback`, see `lifecycle.ts:397-475` — only stack.env,
     portals.compose.yml, custom.compose.yml, stack.state.env are restored).
     A proceed-with-warning path therefore deterministically becomes a worse,
     later failure. The guard runs BEFORE any mutation and throws a
     human-readable, actionable error ("rename to `portal_net` in <path>;
     nothing was changed").
   - The benign case — the user's overlay *defines* `channel_lan` itself
     (top-level `networks:` key), so the merged config still validates — gets
     a **warning**, not an error: surfaced through
     `UpgradeResult.warnings` (currently hardcoded `[]` at
     `lifecycle.ts:524`), logged via `lifecycleLogger.warn`, and printed by
     `openpalm update`.
5. **Fold in docs-cleanup-plan step 5** (`docs-cleanup-plan.md:105-122`):
   rename the health payload `service: channel-${this.name}` →
   `portal-${this.name}` in `packages/portal-sdk/src/base-portal.ts:216`, fix
   the stale `channel-<name>` comment at `base-portal.ts:107`, update the
   assertions at `portals/slack/src/index.test.ts:511` and
   `portals/discord/src/index.test.ts:107`, and update the logger example in
   `docs/technical/bunjs-rules.md` (~line 96) to
   `portal-discord`/`portal-slack`.
6. **Stale comment fixes**: `scripts/dev-e2e-test.sh:123-124`
   ("Channels reach it … over the channel_lan Docker network" → portals /
   `portal_net`). `config-persistence.ts:243` area was verified: it already
   says `portal_net` — no change (verify-only item, done).
7. **Reintroduction grep-gate** in
   `packages/lib/src/control-plane/cleanup-guardrails.test.ts` (the
   established pattern — guardrails 1–9 exist; this adds guardrails 10–11).
8. **CHANGELOG** `[Unreleased]` entries (Removed + Changed).

### Descoped (with justification)

- **Extending `packages/ui/src/lib/server/portals.vitest.ts` with the negative
  case** — would duplicate lib-suite coverage into a consumer suite, which
  `core-principles.md` explicitly forbids (see item 3 above).
- **Docker-gated `docker compose config` validation of the skeleton** — the
  assessment marks it optional; it requires a Docker daemon (not guaranteed in
  the pipeline sandbox). Equivalent structural coverage comes from
  `network-partitioning.test.ts` and `skeleton-guardrail.test.ts`, which parse
  the skeleton YAML and stay green (removing an unreferenced network cannot
  invalidate them — verified: neither file mentions `channel_lan`).
- **Renaming cosmetic "channel" identifiers** in adapter code/tests
  (`DiscordChannel`/`SlackChannel` class names, `openpalm-channel-test-`
  mkdtemp prefixes, Discord/Slack `channelId` fields, the
  `channel-unstaged`/`channel-chat-secret` arbitrary fixture strings in
  `staging.vitest.ts` / `secrets-files.test.ts`) — "channel" there is either a
  platform concept (Discord/Slack channels) or an arbitrary test string, not
  the deprecated OpenPalm portal naming. Out of the issue's scope; churn with
  zero behavior value.
- **Scrubbing historical docs** (0.12.0 CHANGELOG sections, archived reviews,
  0.12.0 roadmap files) — history stays accurate as written.

### 3.2 `packages/lib/src/control-plane/overlay-deprecations.ts` — NEW

Small single-purpose module (no new dependencies; uses `node:fs`, `yaml` —
already a lib dependency — and `customComposeFilePath` from `./home.js`):

```ts
export type ChannelLanScan = { referencedBy: string[]; definesNetwork: boolean };

/** Pure: parse compose YAML content; report services whose `networks` include
 *  channel_lan (list or map form) and whether top-level networks defines it.
 *  Unparseable/non-object input → empty scan (advisory scan, fail-open by
 *  design: compose preflight still hard-fails genuinely broken YAML). */
export function scanComposeForChannelLan(content: string): ChannelLanScan;

/** Read-only check of the user overlay (customComposeFilePath(homeDir)).
 *  Missing file → both null.
 *  referencedBy.length > 0 && !definesNetwork → blockError (merged config
 *    would fail `docker compose config`): names the services, the file path,
 *    instructs renaming to portal_net, and states nothing was changed.
 *  definesNetwork → warning (self-defined network still validates but is
 *    deprecated; suggest renaming to portal_net). */
export function checkCustomComposeChannelLan(homeDir: string): {
  blockError: string | null;
  warning: string | null;
};
```

Type-narrowing style matches `portals.ts` (`unknown` + `typeof … === "object"`
guards; never `any`). NOT exported from the lib barrel (`src/index.ts`) — it is
internal to `reconcileStack`; no external consumer exists, and lib tests import
relatively.

### 3.3 `packages/lib/src/control-plane/lifecycle.ts`

  before `applyHome` can overwrite `core.compose.yml`):

  const overlayCheck = checkCustomComposeChannelLan(state.homeDir);
  if (overlayCheck.blockError) throw new Error(overlayCheck.blockError);

  `reconcileStack` result and pass it through in the returned `UpgradeResult`

## 6. Risks and how the design avoids them

1. **User overlays attached to `channel_lan` hard-fail `docker compose config`
   post-upgrade with zero warning** (assessment risk 1, M7). Avoided: the
   fail-fast guard in `reconcileStack` runs BEFORE the snapshot is armed and
   BEFORE `applyHome` overwrites managed compose files, throwing a
   human-readable rename instruction while the on-disk stack is untouched and
   still running. The benign self-defined-network case degrades to a warning
   surfaced in `UpgradeResult.warnings` and `openpalm update` output.
2. **Skip-version upgrades (0.11.x → 0.13.0) never had CHANNEL_NAME renamed on
   disk; a custom overlay declaring a portal via CHANNEL_NAME silently stops
   being discovered** (assessment risk 2, M6). Mitigation within this task's
   scope: managed compose assets are refreshed from the skeleton (first-party
   files safe by construction); the CHANGELOG Removed entry explicitly states
   `PORTAL_NAME` is the only recognized marker. A content-scan for stray
   `CHANNEL_NAME` markers in user overlays is deliberately NOT added: unlike
   `channel_lan`, a stale `CHANNEL_NAME` cannot take the stack down (compose
   still validates; the service simply is not treated as a portal), and
   guardian gating fails CLOSED for unknown principals — no security regression,
   only a discoverability one, documented in the CHANGELOG.
3. **`service: channel-*` health string is externally observable** (assessment
   risk 3). Grep-verified: no in-repo consumer beyond the two adapter tests.
   The break is called out in the CHANGELOG `### Changed` entry for
   out-of-repo tooling.
4. **Mixed state (new lib, old compose in an existing home)** (assessment
   risk 4). Harmless by design: removing an unused network is compose-inert
   until the managed file is regenerated on the next reconcile; the new marker
   logic and old compose coexist because first-party services already carry
   `PORTAL_NAME` only.
5. **Guard false positives blocking legitimate operations.** Avoided by the
   two-tier design: only the deterministically-fatal case (reference without
   definition) blocks; self-defined networks warn; unparseable YAML yields an
   empty scan (compose preflight remains the authority on YAML validity).

## 7. Out of scope (explicit)

- Any auto-rewrite/migration of `config/stack/custom.compose.yml` (option (b)
  — rejected, § 1 item 4).
- Extending `packages/ui/src/lib/server/portals.vitest.ts` (consumer-suite
  duplication — forbidden by core-principles).
- Renaming platform-concept/cosmetic "channel" identifiers in adapters and
  test fixtures (`DiscordChannel`, `channelId`, mkdtemp prefixes,
  `channel-unstaged`, `channel-chat-secret`).
- Scanning user overlays for stale `CHANNEL_NAME` markers (see risk 2 —
  non-fatal, fail-closed, CHANGELOG-documented instead).
- Docker-daemon-gated `docker compose config` CI check for the skeleton.
- Historical docs/CHANGELOG sections mentioning `channel_lan`/`CHANNEL_NAME`
  (0.12.0 entries, archived reviews, 0.12.0 roadmap).
- Adding `addon_net` to the skeleton README network table (pre-existing gap,
  unrelated to this removal).
- Guardian principal `kind` values, secret naming (`portal_*` prefixes), and
  every other #436-rename surface — already migrated in 0.12.0.
- Barrel-exporting `overlay-deprecations.ts` from `@openpalm/lib` (no external
  consumer; keep the public API surface flat).
